newsitem.title: USA: Weirton, union extend contract deadline.
newsitem.headline: Weirton, union extend contract deadline.

text.p: Weirton Steel Corp said it and the Independent Steelworkers Union Monday agreed to extend the December 15 contract deadline on a day-to-day basis in view of progress on negotiations for a new labor contract.

"The company and the union agreed to a rolling extension, if necessary," said Gregg S. Warren, director-corporate communications. "The tempo of progress accelerated during the weekend but time was becoming an issue. We're hopeful of realizing more progress during negotiations this week."
The extension is the second such agreement made between the parties, the company noted. The first came as the current contract was set to expire September 25, but was extended until December 15.
Warren said the company and the union agreed to the day-to-day extension with the provision that each party give the other at least five days notice if they desire to terminate the arrangement.

"While some difficult issues remain unresolved, progress has been made through strong efforts. The rolling extension certainly is a positive aspect. The company remains reasonably optimistic of reaching a fair and equitable settlement," Warren said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
